sources.title: CDC: Managing Insulin in an Emergency
Meshtastic: Site Planner introduction (antenna height and range)

items.text: **Put the insulin in a working fridge.**
items.note: If there is no power at Gram's, follow the cooling steps in the guide instead. Keep it from freezing.

items.text: **Check blood sugar and the CGM.** Know where the low-sugar supplies and the glucagon are.
items.note: Tell the family where the glucagon is.

items.text: **Check in with the family** by the PACE plan (Comms, then Our plan), and with the out-of-area contact.
items.note: Let people know you arrived safely.

items.text: **Unload in tier order:** medical and must-haves first, then power and comms, then water and food, then the rest.
items.note: Insulin and glucagon go in first.

items.text: **Set up the solar panels in full sun** and connect them to the solar generator.
items.note: Follow the manufacturer's instructions for the cables and connectors.

items.text: **Charge in this order:** medical devices, then phones, then radios, then lights.
items.note: Edit the order if your family agrees on a different one.

items.text: **Find out what water Gram's has:** city, well or stored.
items.note: If it is under an advisory, or you are not sure it is safe, boil or treat it first. Use Map, then Find water, for nearby sources.

items.text: Take stock of the **food, medications and fuel** already at Gram's.
**Put a Meshtastic radio up as high as you can** and send a test message to the rest of the family.
items.note: Raising the antenna is the best way to get more range.

items.text: **Set up the weather radio**, tuned to the frequency shown in Comms, then Listen.
**Agree on a sanitation plan:** toilet, handwashing and trash.
Agree on where everyone sleeps and what you will use for light.
Check that there is a **working carbon monoxide alarm** on every level.
items.note: Run generators and cook outdoors only.

items.text: **Blood sugar and insulin count.** Check sugar and the CGM, and count the insulin you have left.
items.note: Check more often if insulin has been kept warmer than usual.

items.text: **Water left.** Count what is stored and what is safe to drink.
**Generator charge level.** Note what got charged today.

items.note: When in doubt, throw it out.
